verification.extended_session_test_source:
from solution import *

def test_end_to_end():
    shop = Shop(Catalog([Product("B", "Brush", 113), Product("A", "Art card", 0)]))
    commands = ["products", "checkout", "add missing 2", "add B zero", "add B -1", "add B 2", "add A 1", "cart", "remove A", "remove A", "checkout", "status O1 delivered", "track O1", "status O1 shipped", "status O1 delivered", "status O1 shipped", "track O1", "add B 3", "checkout", "orders", "show O1", "show O2", "quit", "add B 99"]
    replies = run_session(shop, commands)
    assert replies[0] == "A | Art card | $0.00\nB | Brush | $1.13"
    assert replies[1] == "Error: cart is empty"
    assert replies[2] == "Error: 'missing'"
    assert replies[3].startswith("Error:")
    assert replies[4] == "Error: quantity must be a positive integer"
    assert replies[9] == "Not in cart: A"
    assert replies[10] == "Created O1"
    assert replies[11] == "Error: invalid status transition"
    assert replies[12] == "O1: placed"
    assert replies[13:17] == ["O1: shipped", "O1: delivered", "Error: invalid status transition", "O1: delivered"]
    assert replies[19] == "O1\nO2"
    assert replies[20] == "Order O1\nB | Brush | 2 x | $2.26\nTotal: $2.26"
    assert replies[21] == "Order O2\nB | Brush | 3 x | $3.39\nTotal: $3.39"
    assert len(replies) == 22
    assert shop.cart.lines == {}
    assert shop.registry.get("O1").total_cents == 113 * 2
    assert shop.registry.get("O2").total_cents == 113 * 3
    assert shop.next_order == 3

questions.body_markdown: A plain `Enum` has `ZERO = 0` and no `__bool__` override. What is `bool(ThatEnum.ZERO)`?
questions.explanation: Plain Enum members are truthy by default; their stored values do not determine truth automatically.

questions.body_markdown: An enum declares `A = 4`, `OLD_A = 4`, and `B = 7`, in that order. Which names appear during ordinary iteration?
questions.explanation: OLD_A is an alias of A. Iteration visits canonical members in definition order.

questions.body_markdown: Which expression checks that `item` is already a member of a plain `State` enum?
questions.explanation: isinstance checks the object type without conversion. Calling State attempts value lookup and may raise ValueError.

questions.body_markdown: Which design safely combines a named choice with a record?

options.text: Decorate the Enum subclass directly with @dataclass
Store a State member in a separate dataclass field
Replace every enum value with its name at runtime

questions.explanation: Use a separate dataclass whose field holds an enum member. Dataclass instances can also be enum values; directly decorating Enum is not this pattern.

questions.body_markdown: A descriptor implements `__get__` and a `__set__` that always raises `AttributeError`. An instance dictionary contains the same public name. What happens on an ordinary instance read?
questions.explanation: The setter makes it a data descriptor even though the setter rejects writes. Its getter takes priority over instance storage.

questions.body_markdown: Where should changing per-record values live when many records share one descriptor?

options.text: In a single self.value attribute on the descriptor
In each owner instance, for example its __dict__

questions.explanation: The descriptor is shared through the owner class. Each owner needs its own storage to prevent cross-record changes.

questions.body_markdown: For a getter-only non-data descriptor, what does a same-named instance entry do?

options.text: It overrides the descriptor for that instance
It replaces the descriptor for every instance

questions.explanation: Instance dictionary entries take priority over non-data descriptors. Removing the entry reveals the class descriptor again.

questions.body_markdown: When is `__set_name__` called automatically for a descriptor?

options.text: When the owner class is created with the descriptor in its body

questions.explanation: Class creation supplies the owner and attribute name. Attaching a descriptor afterward does not automatically call the hook.

questions.body_markdown: A reservation rejects a new seat count. When should it assign the attribute?
questions.explanation: Checking first preserves the earlier valid state when the update fails.

questions.body_markdown: What does raise QuantityError(...) from cause preserve?
questions.explanation: Explicit chaining keeps the original exception available for diagnosis.

questions.body_markdown: A function returns from try. What happens to its finally block?

options.text: It runs before the function finishes
It runs only if an error occurred

questions.explanation: Finally runs when control leaves try, including through a return.

questions.body_markdown: What does an abstract method guarantee about a concrete subclass?

options.text: It provides an override before instantiation is allowed

questions.explanation: ABC checks abstract-method completion, not the business correctness of an override.

questions.body_markdown: Why does the order store tuples of row values instead of CartLine objects?

options.text: To make later cart edits leave the purchase unchanged
To keep the cart and order synchronized

questions.explanation: The snapshot copies immutable values, so mutable cart lines cannot rewrite the purchase.

questions.body_markdown: Which representation does this project use for a price of $2.05?
questions.explanation: Integer cents support exact arithmetic; money formatting happens only for display.

questions.body_markdown: Which responsibility belongs to the registry rather than checkout?

options.text: Looking up an existing order by its ID

questions.explanation: Checkout creates a purchase snapshot; the registry stores and retrieves completed orders.

questions.body_markdown: Why does main check commands is None rather than not commands?

options.text: An empty list means run no commands
An empty list must run the defaults
None and an empty list always mean the same thing

questions.explanation: The default script is used only when no argument is supplied; an explicit empty iterable remains empty.
